Better!

faculty_tidy <- faculty %>%
  select(State, Tier, AvgAssistProfSalary, AvgAssocProfSalary, AvgFullProfSalary) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(AvgAssistProfSalary, AvgAssocProfSalary, AvgFullProfSalary),
    names_to = "Rank",
    values_to = "Salary"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Salary = as.numeric(Salary),
    Rank = recode(Rank,
                  AvgAssistProfSalary = "Assist",
                  AvgAssocProfSalary = "Assoc",
                  AvgFullProfSalary = "Full"),
    Rank = factor(Rank, levels = c("Assist", "Assoc", "Full")),
    Tier = factor(Tier, levels = c("I", "IIA", "IIB"))
  )

head(faculty_tidy)
## # A tibble: 6 × 4
##   State Tier  Rank   Salary
##   <chr> <fct> <fct>   <dbl>
## 1 AK    IIB   Assist    362
## 2 AK    IIB   Assoc     382
## 3 AK    IIB   Full      454
## 4 AK    I     Assist    432
## 5 AK    I     Assoc     560
## 6 AK    I     Full      686
str(faculty_tidy)
## tibble [3,483 × 4] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
##  $ State : chr [1:3483] "AK" "AK" "AK" "AK" ...
##  $ Tier  : Factor w/ 3 levels "I","IIA","IIB": 3 3 3 1 1 1 2 2 2 2 ...
##  $ Rank  : Factor w/ 3 levels "Assist","Assoc",..: 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 2 3 1 ...
##  $ Salary: num [1:3483] 362 382 454 432 560 686 329 494 533 414 ...
faculty_tidy <- faculty_tidy %>%
  filter(!is.na(Tier))

This got rid of the NA

ggplot(faculty_tidy, aes(x = Rank, y = Salary, fill = Rank)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ Tier) +
  labs(
    x = "Rank",
    y = "Salary",
    fill = "Rank"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Task 2: ANOVA

anova_model <- aov(Salary ~ State + Tier + Rank, data = faculty_tidy)

summary(anova_model)
##               Df   Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)    
## State         50  5667124  113342   31.17 <2e-16 ***
## Tier           2  7072361 3536180  972.56 <2e-16 ***
## Rank           2 16526626 8263313 2272.66 <2e-16 ***
## Residuals   3297 11987752    3636                   
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 128 observations deleted due to missingness

State, Tier, and Rank all significantly affect salary (p < 0.001), indicating that salary varies across locations, institution types, and academic ranks.

ggplot(juniper_tidy, aes(x = YearsSinceBurn, y = Concentration)) +
  geom_smooth(se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ ChemicalID, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "YearsSinceBurn",
    y = "Concentration"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Task 5: Linear Model

model_results <- juniper_tidy %>%
  group_by(ChemicalID) %>%
  do(tidy(lm(Concentration ~ YearsSinceBurn, data = .))) %>%
  ungroup()
significant_chemicals <- model_results %>%
  filter(term == "YearsSinceBurn", p.value < 0.05)

significant_chemicals
